steps.content: In the interrogation room, Sumire seems quiet and composed, as if totally unaware of her situation.
The FAC will arrive at the MBCC shortly to perform a special interrogation on Sumire. You still have about 30 minutes, enough time to dig for some info in advance.
Sumire smiles and nods at you when she notices you walking in.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Good day, Chief.
Good day. I've heard a lot about you, Ms Sumire.
I heard your works are very popular among the Eastside dignitaries and have always been in high demand.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: I'm flattered, but it's really nothing worth mentioning. My skills still have a lot of room for improvement.
There's a garden at the Bureau campsite. Feel free to use it during your break.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: I sincerely appreciate that.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Although I don't think you're here today to talk to me about the Bureau's <color=#e45515>Garden</color>, right?
Sumire always wears a friendly smile as she speaks, making her very hard to read.
But you know the FAC's intel is not mistaken. It's highly likely that Sumire works for the assassin organization "the Garden," or at least she knows something about it.
Time is running out. The FAC will be here anytime. No time to beat around the bush anymore.
Can you tell me about the other "Garden"?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: I'll try my best.
test

test

test
This investigation report says the Garden is a secret assassin organization that has existed for a long time. None of its formal members have been exposed or arrested...
Sumire reads through the report carefully several times, even though there is hardly any information on the merely three pages.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: There is no problem with your intelligence.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: But this isn't much information...
There is indeed very little valid information on the report, which is very unusual considering the FAC's intelligence power.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Well, don't be too harsh on those who collect information... The job is way too dangerous for them indeed.
You mean the Garden will kill FAC intelligence officers?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: A secret assassin organization must clear any threats as soon as it can.
Sumire looks as usual with her smile not fading the slightest.
So the Garden dares to take on FAC personnel?
That is the largest official institution in the DisCity, with over ten thousand armed personnel... Countless cases have proven that no Sinner, however powerful and ferocious, can fight it.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: You are right. The FAC is very powerful indeed, and it is very... brutal with Sinners.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: This is exactly why a Sinner assassin organization like the Garden won't avoid them.

options: Is the Garden not afraid that the FAC might retaliate?

choices.text: Is the Garden not afraid that the FAC might retaliate?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: They can't.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: The document is proof that the FAC knows very little about the Garden. They can't get to the Garden with such superficial information.
Is the Garden able to evade the FAC's investigation?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: The Garden is a core organization. Most people don't even know it's the Garden they're working for.
What about those within the organization? Have you guys not failed at all?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: As far as I know...

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Yes.

options: How long has the Garden been around?

choices.text: How long has the Garden been around?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Longer than any other assassin organization in the DisCity.
Sumire's answer sends chills down your spine. This means that this extremely dangerous assassin organization has existed for years without anyone realizing it.

options: Do <color=#e45515>you guys</color> have special ways to assassinate?

choices.text: Do <color=#e45515>you guys</color> have special ways to assassinate?

steps.content: Sumire blinks and makes no comment on how you're addressing her differently.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: The Garden is a Sinner organization...
The dangerous and unpredictable abilities of Sinners can indeed hide a lot of important information. But this answer is still too general.
You have another file, which can help narrow down the Garden assassin's identity.

It's a name list of FAC members who died in accidents in recent years. Sumire picks it up, and this time, she flips through it very quickly. It takes her less than two minutes to read the pile of lists.
She closes the file after flipping through it and looks at you again.

options: Talk about what happened on May 30

choices.text: Talk about what happened on May 30

steps.content: Wiese Momoa. Died of heart failure around 4:00 a.m. on May 30.
Liszt Lampard. Died in a car accident at 8:51 a.m. on May 30.
Dylan. Died of drowning around 9:00 p.m. on May 30.
These causes of death don't seem suspicious, but having three FAC officers dying on the same day is extremely unusual in itself.
This is also what the FAC's intelligence officer highlighted in the report as "cases most likely to be assassinations by the Garden."

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: These people were indeed targeted by the Garden.
Sumire answers before you ask her, as if she knows what question you have in mind.
How?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: It isn't difficult. It simply requires experience and patience.
Surely it requires much more to assassinate that many FAC officers and keep unnoticed.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: We also have the most convenient and secretive tool... Sinners' abilities.
...So it was you who killed these people?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: No. According to the Garden's rules, I don't deal with commissions of this level.
What level of people do you deal with then?
Sumire simply smiles and fixates her gentle gaze on you without giving an answer. Her expression sends chills down your spine for some reason and stops you from pressing further.
After a moment of silence, you ask your next question.
Your sudden question makes Sumire show a rare look of slight confusion. She seems to be baffled by why you have asked such a question.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: The Garden is the best assassin organization. They won't be overly picky when it comes to commission targets.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Besides, the target is the FAC, which basically all Sinners hate. The Garden has the ability and intention to complete these commissions.
I'm not asking why you guys are assassinating FAC staff.
You are a "core member of the Garden," right? Your organization doesn't have a record of simply revealing information about yourselves like this.
Do you wish to be a state witness? Did you fall out with the Garden? Or did you deliberately get caught to set up some kind of trap? Why are you here?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: No, I love and respect everyone in the Garden.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: See it as a... warning if you wish to believe so.
A warning? That I should let you go? Or that the Garden is going to kill me?
Your questions take Sumire by surprise for a moment, but then a smile quickly returns to her face.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: All I hope is that... you and the FAC will stop investigating the Garden.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: You won't achieve anything other than provoking the Garden.
Is the Garden going to confront the FAC openly?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: "Going to" isn't quite the right word. The Garden has always seen the FAC as an enemy.
But you've revealed so much crucial information already—your assassin identity and the garden's ways of doing things.
Considering your past identity as an ikebana artist in Eastside, we will be able to identify more assassins from the Garden with a large-scale screening.
With your identities exposed, Are assassins like you still able to threaten the FAC?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Maybe not, if it's just us.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: But the Garden has a real trump card.
What kind of trump card?
There's a hint of hesitation on her face. But after a moment, Sumire gives a name.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: ...The Mentor.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: ...She's a true ikebana artist, the master of the Garden.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: It is she who gives new life to each flower.
The Garden dares to fight against the whole FAC with just one person?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Yes.
Sumire doesn't hesitate the slightest when answering this question.
That's impossible.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: ...You haven't met the Mentor, so you won't understand how strong her power is.
Tension lingers in the room for a moment. You heave a deep sigh.
You just said you loved and respected your fellows in the Garden, right?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Yes.
So what do you think of the FAC?

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: I don't like killing people if I'm not commissioned to.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: I prefer to spend my time practicing ikebana... Unfortunately, I had made my choice a long time ago.
Although Sumire hasn't said so explicitly, her attitude is evident—She doesn't particularly hate the FAC.
In that case, I hope you will give me all the information about the Garden honestly.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Why?
This time it's Sumire asking.
The FAC already knows about the Garden and is planning to deal with you guys. As you know, the FAC can be very... radical toward Sinners.
Sumire nods in agreement with your statement.
If you give me more information about the Garden and the Mentor, I'll be able to take in the other Sinners before the FAC does.
And with the power of the Bureau and the shackles, I'll be able to stop a bigger conflict from breaking out.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: You're always so... kind.
Kindness isn't really a desirable quality in this world.
I just want to prevent unnecessary sacrifices, whether that's in the FAC or the Garden.
The smile on Sumire's face becomes somewhat bitter. After a long silence, she lets out a soft sigh.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Please forgive me for not being able to say yes.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: I've told you too much information indeed, some of which was even related to the core of the Garden. But it was all because...
Sumire pauses.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: I can't betray the Garden.
The situation is already out of your control.
The FAC special commissioner is arriving soon. If they force you with truth serum and torturing, I won't even have the authority to intervene.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: I'm telling you all these information as an ikebana artist.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: When facing the FAC... the creations of the Garden do not speak. Don't worry.
That's not what I'm worried about, of course...

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Besides, he might not be able to make it here.
Not able to make it here? What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, the Commissioner's car will arrive soon. A request is sent to let him in.
Sumire's interrogation remains unresolved. You stand up somewhat irritably and pick up the files on the desk to meet the FAC commissioner.
An envelope slips out of the files and drift onto the floor.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: These are...?
You ponder for a few seconds but fail to recall where the letter comes from.
It isn't in the directory, so it probably belongs to a staff member.

steps.speaker: Sumire
steps.content: Can I... have a look?

You pick it up and find elegant handwriting on the back of the envelope that writes: "To Sumire." A full moon is stamped on the purple wax.
So this is yours?
Sumire doesn't answer and opens the letter.
You glance at the letter and see only one sentence—"The return is nigh. Gather the flowers while you can."
...Sumire?
You want to ask some questions when you notice her usual calm and gentle smile has disappeared from her face.
Are you okay?
Sumire remains silent and motionless, holding the letter in her hand.

choices.text: Is there something wrong with this letter?

options: "The return is nigh. Gather the flowers while you can." What does it mean?

choices.text: "The return is nigh. Gather the flowers while you can." What does it mean?

steps.content: Sumire is still silent, with her face even paler than the letter sheet.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief. We have an emergency.
Nightingale's voice suddenly rings out over the comms.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: That FAC Commissioner... is dead.
What happened?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Only after pulling up did the driver realize that the commissioner had already died in the back seat.
Your mind goes blank. This is completely beyond expectations. You take a few dozen seconds to make sense of the situation.
Even though Sumire is acting very suspiciously, there are more important things to get on with.
You shoot Sumire a glance, whose face remains pale.
You just said the commissioner might not even make it here...
No, wait. You had been here with me the whole time. There was no way you could kill...
I will figure it all out—everything about the Garden, who the Mentor is, and... what you're trying to achieve.
Sumire still doesn't respond, but her gaze becomes determined the moment you turn away.
